threads.body: These two static imports both introduce the simple name `SECONDS`: `Constants.SECONDS` is the unit `String` `"s"`, while `TimeUnit.SECONDS` is the enum constant. Both are actually used — `TimeUnit.SECONDS` in `latch.await(10, SECONDS)` (line 50) and `Constants.SECONDS` in `.hasUnit(SECONDS)` (line 57). Because two different members named `SECONDS` are in scope, every use of the simple name `SECONDS` is an ambiguous reference and the `testJava21` source set will fail to compile, so this test can never run. Keep one as a static import and reference the other in qualified form, e.g. keep `import static java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit.SECONDS;`, replace the `Constants.SECONDS` static import with a regular `import io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.runtimetelemetry.internal.Constants;`, and change line 57 to `.hasUnit(Constants.SECONDS)`.
